CLIPPING_AND_OVERLAP.measured: Proved at the strongest available level. The delivered canonical page content stream is 23366 bytes and decomposes exactly into: the two bytes 'q\n', then the source page's own 22096-byte content stream byte-for-byte at offset 2, then 1268 trailing bytes whose only operators are q, cm, Do and Q - fifteen widget placements and nothing else. FILING_DESTINATION.measured: The guide names the destination the route names and gives the statutory basis: 'File with the clerk of the court in which the conviction was entered, in the underlying criminal proceeding. That is section 2264(1) and it is what the committed manifest and the committed track record both say. It is not a new case; it is a motion in the old one.' It then tells the participant to tick the matching court at the head of the form and to check the county and docket number the platform wrote into the caption against the judgment. The filing channel is not overstated: the guide says eFiling availability depends on the county's place in the Maine eCourts rollout and that the record holds this unresolved and moving, which matches the registry's own nonblocking research note.

FEE_AND_WAIVER.measured: Both stated, and both are the committed manifest's own words, present verbatim in the guide. Fee: 'No fee is expected. Administrative Order JB-05-26 (A. 3-26), effective 9 March 2026, lists no fee for a criminal post-judgment motion and provides Filing a Criminal Action, Traffic Infraction, or Civil Violation: No fee in both Superior and District Court.' The guide additionally disposes of the 60 dollar figure by its own terms - tied to M.R. Civ. P. 55(b)(2), 59, 60(b), 62 and 66, which are civil rules - and tells the participant to confirm with the clerk and not to expect a refund. Waiver: the manifest's position is printed whole, including the instruction not to route the participant to CV-067 or CV-191 because those are civil in-forma-pauperis forms and the application of M.R. Civ. P. 91 to a criminal motion is unresolved. The absence of a waiver form in the packet is stated as deliberate and explained, rather than being a silent gap.

SERVICE.measured: Recipient and method are both answered, and the one thing the record does not settle is disclosed rather than guessed. The guide states that CR-218 carries no certificate of service and that the packet adds none, that the committed manifest records no service obligation imposed on the movant by the statute or the form, and that section 2264(3) directs notice to the prosecutorial office that represented the State but does not assign the act to the movant. It then gives the participant an action that closes the gap either way: ask the clerk at the counter whether the prosecutor needs a copy, and offer a courtesy copy if asked. That is the treatment the committed track registry prescribes in its own words ('The packet fails closed: it tells the participant that the court is understood to give notice, and that they should confirm with the clerk at filing and deliver a courtesy copy if the clerk asks'). Verified against the registry: the service question is recorded with impact 'release_blocker', buildBlockers is empty, and MASTER_QUEUE records legalInputStatus SETTLED - so this is a completeness PASS over a family that still carries a counsel release blocker, and the two must not be confused. See releaseBlockerCarried below.

SELF_HELP_STOP.measured: The strongest of the four families read this shift. The committed track registry carries 11 selfHelpStopConditions and the guide's 'When to stop and get help' list carries all 11, in the registry's order and substance - unclear offence class, the Class D marijuana mapping, an uncertain completion date or unpaid balance, any post-completion case anywhere, a deferred disposition, an older Maine prior, non-citizenship, wanting to challenge the conviction, the State signalling opposition, a previous denial, and firearm rights. The guide also states the boundary of the product itself in 'What this packet is not': not legal advice, not filed for you, does not decide eligibility under 15 M.R.S. section 2261(6), not expungement ('Maine does not have expungement'), not a proposed order, and not a motion for a non-conviction record. It refuses to sign, refuses the eligibility characterisation, and hands the section 2264(7) post-grant reporting duty back to the participant in terms.

observationsFromTheBytes.what: Two cross-references in participant-instructions.md point at a section on CR-218 paragraph 3 that the delivered document does not contain, and the both-readings explanation the builder's own contract commits to is not in the delivered guide.
observationsFromTheBytes.measured: participant-instructions.md carries fifteen headings and none of them is a paragraph 3 section. Line 118 reads 'Paragraph 3 is the one to slow down on - see the section below.' Line 138 reads 'CR-218 paragraph 3 and 15 M.R.S. section 2262(3) do not agree, and the committed record says the answer is outcome-determinative. See the section on paragraph 3.' There is no such section. The builder's own header at scripts/build-census-v1-me-seal-gen-set.mjs lines 66 to 87 states the intended treatment - 'the packet sets out both readings in plain terms' - and the delivered guide never states what paragraph 3 asserts ('Defendant has no other adult criminal convictions in Maine and has not had a case dismissed as the result of a deferred disposition since completing their sentence for this offense'), never states what section 2262(3) bars, and never states the defect itself: that the trailing time limit governs the deferred-disposition clause but not the convictions clause, so a participant with an old prior predating the completion date is not disqualified by the statute but reads as disqualified on the form.
observationsFromTheBytes.consequence: The participant is not misdirected into filing blind - the disagreement is named twice, called outcome-determinative, and carried into the stop list as 'you have an older Maine prior that predates the completion date' - so SELF_HELP_STOP and REQUIRED_BEFORE_FILING both hold on their terms and this is not scored against any of the fifteen. It is still a defect in a delivered participant document: a reader following either pointer finds nothing, on the item the packet itself calls outcome-determinative.
observationsFromTheBytes.repair: In scripts/build-census-v1-me-seal-gen-set.mjs, either add the paragraph 3 section the two pointers promise - quoting CR-218 paragraph 3 as the form prints it, quoting what 15 M.R.S. section 2262(3) actually bars, and stating the mismatch the track registry records - or remove both pointers. The section is the better repair, because the builder's header already says setting out both readings is the treatment and the registry already carries the material.

observationsFromTheBytes.what: A builder-hardcoded sentence in participant-instructions.md states a component count and names a component that neither committed record declares, and attributes its reasoning to a registry that does not carry it.
observationsFromTheBytes.measured: Line 108 of the delivered guide reads: 'The three `process_guidance` components are carried in this document rather than as separate PDFs. The committed track registry records why: the record-gathering step is preparation before filing and the follow-through step is ordinary post-filing handoff, so neither is a legally distinct unit. The good-character affidavit request is guidance for the same reason...'. Measured against the records the packet binds to: the committed packet-set manifest for me-seal-gen-set declares TWO components, one official_pdf_fill (CR-218) and ONE process_guidance (me-seal-gen-instructions-2); the committed track registry declares the same two and contains the string 'process_guidance' exactly once. Searched across the whole track registry entry: 'legally distinct' 0 hits, 'record-gathering' 0 hits, 'follow-through' 0 hits, 'good character' 0 hits, 'good-character' 0 hits. The registry's only postGenerationHandoffs entry is about the mandatory hearing. The packet's own component table, printed two lines above the sentence, shows exactly the two declared components. The sentence is hard-coded at scripts/build-census-v1-me-seal-gen-set.mjs lines 1899 to 1902 and is not read from any record.
observationsFromTheBytes.consequence: No declared component is missing and no filing step is misstated, so COMPONENT_SET holds. But this is a false statement of fact in a participant-facing document whose own stated method is that nothing in it is the packet's restatement of the record, and it names a good-character affidavit request that appears nowhere in this packet, in neither committed record, and nowhere in chapter 310-A. It reads as text carried over from another jurisdiction's builder.
observationsFromTheBytes.repair: In scripts/build-census-v1-me-seal-gen-set.mjs lines 1899 to 1902, replace the hard-coded sentence with one derived from the manifest's own components array, or delete it. If the sentence stays in any form it must not claim a count the manifest does not carry, must not name a good-character affidavit request, and must not attribute the reasoning to the committed track registry unless the registry carries it.
